# Setting SETTLE and KANERVA up

## What you need first

`rustc` and `cargo`, to build SETTLE and KANERVA. Install Rust from rustup.rs; settle-mcp never runs an installer.

`git`, only to fetch from a git URL. Node 18 or newer, to run settle-mcp itself.

`check_system` runs `rustc --version`, `cargo --version` and `git --version` and reports each one, and asks a `settle` or `kanerva` that is already built for its `--version`. It runs nothing else.

## Where the code comes from

settle-mcp has no default source and never guesses one. Give it a local folder (a clone of SETTLE, or a folder that holds the `settle-rs` crate) or a git URL, such as `https://github.com/triplesparkle/SETTLE`, which is public. KANERVA is found where `settle-rs/Cargo.toml` names it by path (`../kanerva`); SETTLE's own repository names KANERVA by its git URL instead, so with it pass `kanerva_source` as well (`https://github.com/triplesparkle/KANERVA`).

A git source is cloned with `git clone --depth 1`. The SETTLE and KANERVA repositories are public; a private repository you name instead asks for your credentials at that step, and the step reports git's own words if access is refused.

## Read the plan, then run it

The first `setup` call is a dry run. It returns every step with the exact command and a plan id, and runs nothing.

The second call repeats the arguments with `dry_run` false and `confirm` set to the plan id. Any changed argument changes the id, so the commands that run are the commands you read.

## What setup does

Check `rustc` and `cargo` (and `git` for a git source). Make the folder. Copy each crate without `target/` and `.git/`, or clone it. Run `cargo build --release` in `settle-rs`, and `cargo build --release --bins --example quickstart` in `kanerva`, which builds the `kanerva` command and the quickstart example.

Verify: the built `settle` runs a tested core example and a tested sdm example from its own `docs/examples/`, the `kanerva` command runs one of its own `programs/*.kanerva`, and each output must match the stored `.out` byte for byte. Then the folder and both binary paths are written to `~/.settle-mcp/state.json` (or `SETTLE_MCP_STATE`).

`setup` waits up to `wait_seconds` (default 50, at most 55, because many clients stop waiting for a call after 60 seconds) and then returns while the build goes on; `setup_status` reports each step as it finishes.

## What it never does

It never uses `sudo` or another privileged command; the command runner refuses one. It never runs an installer, never edits a shell profile, and writes only inside your folder and its one state file. It never invents a public URL.

## A build you already have

Set `SETTLE_BIN` to a built `settle` binary and `KANERVA_BIN` to a built `kanerva`, or `SETTLE_MCP_HOME` to a folder holding a built `settle-rs/` and `kanerva/`. Every usage tool also takes the paths directly.
